parts.text:
Three data values are $x = 48,\; 51,\; 56$. Each value is coded using $y = x - 50$.
(i) State the three values of $y$.
(ii) Calculate the mean of $y$ and hence find the mean of $x$.

For $n = 20$ observations of a variable $x$, it is given that $\sum (x - 15) = 80$.
(i) State the relationship between $\sum (x - 15)$ and $\sum x$.
(ii) Calculate $\sum x$ and the mean of $x$.
For $25$ values, let $y = x - a$ where $a$ is a constant. Given that $\sum y = 150$ and $\sum y^2 = 1900$, calculate the variance and standard deviation of $x$.

questions.title: Recovering Totals from Mean and Standard Deviation

parts.text:
Eight values have a mean of $12.5$ and a standard deviation of $3.5$.
Find the value of $\sum x$ and the value of $\sum x^2$.

questions.title: Updating a Mean When One New Value Joins

parts.text:
Seven monthly prices have a mean of $250\text{ dollars}$. When one new price is added, the mean of all eight prices becomes $245\text{ dollars}$.
Calculate the value of the new price.

For $15$ observations of a variable $x$, it is given that $\sum (x - a) = 0$, where $a$ is a constant.
(i) Show that $a$ must equal the mean of $x$.
(ii) State whether $\sum (x - a)^2$ equals the variance of $x$, giving a brief reason.

questions.title: Coding Raw Decimal Values Around a Base

parts.text:
Six measurements are:
$$998.5,\; 1001.2,\; 1000.3,\; 999.8,\; 1002.2,\; 999.0$$
Using the code $y = x - 1000$, find the six values of $y$ and calculate the mean of $x$.
Calculate $\sum y^2$, and hence find the standard deviation of $x$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Finding the Shift Constant from Coded Totals

parts.text:
For $40$ values of $x$, let $y = x - a$, where $a$ is a constant. It is given that $\sum y = 360$ and $\sum y^2 = 4840$.
Calculate the variance and standard deviation of $x$.
Given further that the mean of $x$ is $59.0$, find the value of the constant $a$ and determine $\sum x$.

For $16$ values of $x$, it is given that $\bar{x} = 28$, $\sum (x - 20) = 128$, and $\sum (x - 20)^2 = 1664$.
Verify that the coded mean is consistent with $\bar{x}$, and find the variance of $x$.
By equating the variance of $x$ to $\frac{\sum x^2}{16} - (\bar{x})^2$, calculate the value of $\sum x^2$.

questions.title: Recovering Coded Sum from Variance and Squared Total

parts.text:
For $30$ values of $x$, let $y = x - 40$. It is given that $\sum y^2 = 1350$, the standard deviation of $x$ is $3$, and $\sum y > 0$.
Calculate $\sum y$.
Hence find the mean of $x$ and the value of $\sum x^2$.

questions.title: Grouped Data Standard Deviation and Shift Coding

parts.text:
The completion times, $t$ minutes, for $20$ tasks are grouped as follows:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{Time } (t \text{ minutes}) & \text{Frequency } (f) \\ \hline 0 \le t < 10 & 4 \\ 10 \le t < 20 & 8 \\ 20 \le t < 30 & 6 \\ 30 \le t < 50 & 2 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
State the midpoints $m$ of the four classes and calculate the estimated mean completion time.
Calculate $\sum f m^2$, and hence estimate the standard deviation of the task completion times, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Combined Mean and Standard Deviation of Two Groups

parts.text:
Group $A$ consists of $12$ scores with mean $42$ and standard deviation $5$.
Group $B$ consists of $8$ scores with mean $54$ and standard deviation $4$.
Calculate the combined mean of all $20$ scores.
Calculate the sum of squares $\sum x^2$ for Group $A$ and for Group $B$, and hence state the combined sum of squares $\sum x_{\text{comb}}^2$ for all $20$ scores.

Calculate the combined variance and the combined standard deviation of all $20$ scores, giving the standard deviation correct to 3 significant figures. Explain why the combined standard deviation exceeds the standard deviation of each individual group.

questions.title: Comprehensive Examination Synthesis: Mixed Summaries and Three New Values

parts.text:
Set $A$ contains $10$ measurements with mean $30$ and standard deviation $4$.
Set $B$ contains $5$ measurements with $\sum y = 180$ and $\sum y^2 = 6600$.
Calculate the combined mean $\bar{x}_{\text{comb}}$ of all $15$ measurements.
Calculate $\sum x^2$ for Set $A$, and hence find the combined standard deviation of all $15$ measurements in Sets $A$ and $B$, correct to 3 significant figures.

Three new measurements, $14,\; 20,\; 23$, join a separate group of $9$ measurements that had $\sum x = 153$ and $\sum x^2 = 2661$.
Calculate the mean and standard deviation of all $12$ measurements.
